Unified sample size calculator (three-axis API)

Source: R/calculate.R
calculate.Rd

Computes sample size (or events/cases) for a study design identified by the triple design / task / outcome. See the installed reference manual system.file("reference", "DESIGN_MATRIX.md", package = "SampleSizeCalc") for the complete combination table, formulas, and literature sources (also on the pkgdown site under reference/).

Usage

calculate(...)

Arguments

...

... Control and design arguments, resolved by EXACT name (partial matching is deliberately avoided so that design-specific arguments such as d cannot be swallowed by the design slot).

**Control arguments**

* `design` (first positional argument): one of `"rct"`, `"paired"`,
  `"rctSingleArm"`, `"crossover"`, `"bioequivalence"`,
  `"singleArmPhaseII"`, `"cohort"`, `"caseControl"`,
  `"caseControlMatched"`, `"crosstab"`, `"singleProportion"`,
  `"singleMean"`, `"singleCorrelation"`, `"diagAccuracy"`,
  `"diagAccuracyCompare"`, `"diagAUC"`, `"diagAUCCompare"`, `"diagLR"`,
  `"clusterRCT"`, `"steppedWedge"`, `"twoOrdinal"`, `"predictiveModel"`,
  `"kappa"`, `"its"` - the study-design axis.
* `task` (second positional argument): `"test"`, `"estimate"`,
  `"noninferiority"`, `"superiority"`, `"equivalence"`, or `"plan"`;
  optional for unambiguous designs.
* `outcome` (third positional argument): `"mean"`, `"proportion"`,
  `"rate"`, `"survival"`, `"auc"`, `"lr"`, `"correlation"`, `"ordinal"`,
  or `"events"`; optional for unambiguous designs.
* `alpha`: scalar in (0, 1), default 0.05. Use 0.025 for one-sided
  non-inferiority trials spending a full two-sided 0.05.
* `power`: scalar in (0, 1), default 0.8 (80 percent); 0.9 for
  confirmatory trials.
* `alternative`: `"one.sided"` (the package's historical default and the
  Akoglu 2022 Table 2 Eq 2 convention) or `"two.sided"` (Hajian-Tilaki
  2014 Eq 6.8 convention), or `NULL` to keep the design default.
  Currently consumed by `diagAccuracy` + `test` + `proportion` only;
  Supplying it for an unsupported design raises an error.
* `dropout`: anticipated dropout/non-response proportion in &lbrack;0, 1),
  inflating by 1/(1-d). Currently applied by `cohort` + `test` +
  `proportion` only; supplying it elsewhere raises an error.
  Unknown or unused design-specific arguments also raise an error.

**Design-specific parameters** (all validated; ranges shown):

* *RCT, test, mean*: `mean1`, `mean2` real-valued group means (e.g.
  mmHg); `sd` > 0 pooled standard deviation.
* *RCT, test, proportion*: `p1`, `p2` in (0, 1) response rates, must
  differ.
* *RCT, test, survival*: `hr` in (0, 1) anticipated hazard ratio
  (<1 = benefit); `pE` in (0, 1) experimental-arm share (default 0.5).
  Returns **events** required.
* *RCT, noninferiority/superiority, mean or proportion*: same inputs as
  above plus `margin` > 0 (NI margin Delta, one-sided alpha; or the
  minimal clinically important difference for superiority).
* *RCT, equivalence, mean or proportion*: `margin` = corridor
  half-width; must exceed |mean1 - mean2| (or |p1 - p2|); uses
  Z_(beta/2).
* *paired*: optional `pairing = "within_subject"` (default) counts
  one distinct person per complete pair of observations;
  `"matched_subjects"` counts two distinct people per pair.
  `n_measurements` always counts two observations per pair.
* *paired, mean*: `meanDiff` != 0 within-subject mean difference;
  `sdDiff` > 0 SD of the differences (NOT the pooled SD).
* *paired, proportion*: `p1`, `p2` in (0, 1); `psi` in (0, 1) expected
  discordant-pair proportion, psi >= |p1-p2|; output in pairs.
* *rctSingleArm, mean*: `mu0` historical mean, `mu1` anticipated mean,
  `sigma` > 0.
* *rctSingleArm, proportion*: `p0` historical rate, `p1` anticipated
  rate, both in (0, 1).
* *crossover, mean*: `delta` > 0 treatment difference; `sigma_within` > 0
  within-subject SD.
* *bioequivalence*: `cv` in (0, 1) intra-subject CV; `theta0` GMR inside
  the acceptance range (default 1.0); `margin_low`/`margin_high` default
  0.8/1.25 (80-125 rule).
* *singleArmPhaseII*: `p0` unacceptable rate; `p1` > p0 target rate;
  `optimizer` = "optimal" or "minimax".
* *cohort, proportion*: `p0`, `p1` in (0, 1); `ratio` >= 1
  unexposed:exposed; optional `dropout` in &lbrack;0, 1) inflates by 1/(1-d).
* *cohort, rate*: `rate0`, `rate1` > 0 events per person-time; `ratio`
  at least  1 person-time ratio.
* *caseControl*: `p0` in (0, 1) control exposure rate; `OR` > 0, != 1;
  `m` >= 1 controls per case (default 1).
* *caseControlMatched*: `p0`, `OR` as above; 1:1 matching built in.
* *crosstab*: `p0`, `p1` in (0, 1) prevalence in unexposed/exposed.
* *singleProportion*: `p` in (0, 1); `precision` > 0; `precision_type` =
  "absolute" (default) or "relative".
* *singleMean*: `sigma` > 0; `precision` > 0 margin of error.
* *singleCorrelation*: `r` in (0, 1); exactly one of `precision`
  (absolute CI half-width in (0, 1)) or `epsilon` (relative).
* *diagAccuracy, estimate*: `prob` in (0, 1) expected Se/Sp; `d` in
  (0, 1) CI half-width; `prevalence` in (0, 1&rbrack;; optional `ci_method` =
  "precision" (Zhou Eq 6.2) or "ci_width_power" (Eq 6.1, uses `power`).
* *diagAccuracy, test*: `prob`, `p0` in (0, 1); `method` = "asymptotic"
  or "exact" (one-sided A'Hern; a two-sided request errors).
  Dual-endpoint planning adds `prob_spec`, `p0_spec`, `dual = TRUE`,
  and `dual_power` (default 0.90 per endpoint). Cases and non-cases
  have separate quotas; screening is the maximum of the prevalence-
  adjusted quotas in expectation. Omit prevalence for separate strata.
* *diagAccuracyCompare*: `p1`, `p2` in (0, 1); `paired` = TRUE requires
  `psi` in (0, 1); margin tasks add `margin` in (0, 1).
* *diagAUC, estimate/test and diagAUCCompare, test*: optional `ratio` > 0
  means controls per case (non-cases:cases; default 1). Alternatively,
  supply `prevalence` in (0, 1) for clinical recruitment, with
  R = (1-prevalence)/prevalence. Supply only one of these arguments.
  `var_method` defaults to `"binormal"`; alternatives are
  `"exponential"` and `"conservative"`. Fixed quotas return
  `controls_needed` and `total_subjects`; `total_subjects_to_screen`
  is present only for clinical recruitment and is expectation-based.
  Historical `prevalence = 1` selects the default 1:1 quota.
* *diagAUC, estimate*: `auc` in (0, 1); `d` > 0.
* *diagAUC, test*: `auc`, `auc0` in (0, 1), auc > auc0.
* *diagAUCCompare*: `auc1`, `auc2` in (0, 1); `r` in &lbrack;0, 1) (default
  0.5); margin tasks add `margin` in (0, 1).
* *diagLR, estimate*: `sens`, `spec` in (0, 1); `lr_type` = "positive"
  or "negative"; `target_lr` > 0 the boundary the CI must not cross.
* *clusterRCT*: base two-group args plus `icc` in &lbrack;0, 1) and
  `cluster_size` integer >= 1 (DE = 1 + (m-1)*ICC).
* *steppedWedge*: `theta` != 0; `tau2` > 0; `sigma2_ind` > 0; `m` >= 1;
  `n_clusters` integer >= 2, a multiple of `clusters_per_step` >= 1.
* *twoOrdinal*: `or` > 0, != 1; `prop_bar` positive vector summing to 1.
* *predictiveModel, binary*: `prev` in (0, 1); `n_parameters` integer
  at least  1; `r2_cs` within its feasible maximum; `shrinkage` default 0.9;
  `mape` default 0.05; `precision_delta` default 0.05.
* *predictiveModel, rate*: `rate` > 0 per person-year; `timepoint` > 0;
  `precision_delta` in (0, 1); optional `n_parameters`/`epv` cross-check.
* *predictiveModel, events*: `n_parameters` >= 1; `epv` >= 1 (classic
  10); `event_prevalence` in (0, 1).
* *predictiveModel, plan, binary*: `prev` in (0, 1), positive integer
  `n_parameters`, and anticipated adjusted Cox-Snell `r2_cs` below its
  prevalence-specific maximum. `shrinkage` defaults to 0.9 and must
  exceed `r2_cs` and be below 1; `precision_delta` defaults to 0.05.
  The returned size meets B1 (outcome precision), B3 (shrinkage), and
  B4 (Nagelkerke R-squared optimism at most 0.05). `mape` defaults to
  0.05 and is informational for at most 30 predictor parameters;
  it does not constrain the returned size.
* *kappa, estimate*: `pi1`, `pi2` in (0, 1); `kappa` in &lbrack;0, 1); `d` in
  (0, 1).
* *kappa, test*: `kappa1` != `kappa2` in (0, 1); same pi's.
* *its*: `effect_sd` > 0; `n_pre`, `n_post` integers >= 3 (>= 8
  recommended); `rho` in &lbrack;0, 1). Returns achieved power.

Value

Object of class sample_size_result with print, summary, and plot methods. Default printing shows sample sizes, the plain-text formula (formula), LaTeX source (formula_latex), calculation process (calculation_steps, also available as calculation), and literature references (reference). New-style objects also carry axis metadata (task, outcome, design_canonical, results, roles, adjustments). summary.sample_size_result() additionally lists all input parameters and recorded adjustments.

Examples

# Antihypertensive RCT: placebo 10 mmHg vs new drug 12 mmHg SBP reduction,
# pooled SD 3 mmHg, two-sided alpha 0.05, 80% power
calculate("rct", "test", "mean", mean1 = 10, mean2 = 12, sd = 3)
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results
#> • Design type: "Two independent samples, mean comparison"
#> • Sample size per group: 37
#> • Total sample size: 74
#> Formula (plain text):
#> `n = 2 * ((Z_alpha/2 + Z_beta) * sd / (mean1 - mean2))^2`
#> Formula (LaTeX):
#> $$n = 2\left(\frac{Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}}{\delta}\right)^2 = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha/2} + Z_{\beta}) \cdot \sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2}\right)^2$$ 
#> Calculation process:
#> 
#> • Step 1: State hypotheses: H0: mu1 = mu2 vs H1: mu1 != mu2 (two-sided alpha =
#> 0.05, power = 0.80).
#> • Step 2: Calculate mean difference delta = |mu1 - mu2| = |10 - 12| = 2; common
#> SD sigma = 3.
#> • Step 3: Determine critical values: Z_(alpha/2) = 1.96 (for two-sided alpha =
#> 0.05), Z_beta = 0.8416 (for power = 0.80).
#> • Step 4: Compute initial sample size via normal approximation: n0 = 2 *
#> ((Z_(alpha/2) + Z_beta) * sigma / delta)^2 = 2 * ((1.96 + 0.8416) * 3 / 2)^2 =
#> 35.32.
#> • Step 5: Refine via exact two-sample Student's t-test power iteration
#> (accounting for degrees of freedom df = 2n - 2).
#> • Step 6: Round up to integer: n = 37 per group, total sample size N = 74.
#> Reference:
#> Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). Sample Size Calculations in Clinical Research (3rd ed.). CRC Press. Chapter 3 (Comparing Means), Section 3.2.1 two-sample parallel design, Eq 3.11 (p. 48; the Student t refinement is Table 3.2, p. 49).
#> 
#>  Also: Machin et al. (2018) Eq 5.4, p. 69 (same formula with the Student t correction term). 
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 

# Generic vs originator antidiabetic, non-inferiority margin 1 point,
# one-sided alpha 0.05
calculate(
  design = "rct", task = "noninferiority", outcome = "mean",
  mean1 = 10, mean2 = 9.5, sd = 3, margin = 1
)
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results
#> • Design type: "Non-inferiority (means)"
#> • Sample size per group: 50
#> • Total sample size: 100
#> Formula (plain text):
#> `n = 2*(Z_a+Z_b)^2*sd^2/(mean1-mean2+margin)^2`
#> Formula (LaTeX):
#> $$n = 2\left(\frac{(Z_{\alpha} + Z_{\beta})\sigma}{\mu_1 - \mu_2 + \Delta}\right)^2$$ 
#> Calculation process:
#> 
#> • Step 1: State non-inferiority hypotheses: H0: mu1 - mu2 <= -margin vs H1: mu1
#> - mu2 > -margin (margin Delta = 1, one-sided alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80).
#> • Step 2: Effective difference: delta_E = mu1 - mu2 + margin = 10 - 9.50 + 1 =
#> 1.50; SD sigma = 3.
#> • Step 3: Determine critical values: one-sided Z_alpha = 1.6449, Z_beta =
#> 0.8416.
#> • Step 4: Compute sample size: n = 2 * (Z_alpha + Z_beta)^2 * sigma^2 /
#> delta_E^2 = 2 * (1.6449 + 0.8416)^2 * 3^2 / (1.50)^2 = 49.46.
#> • Step 5: Round up to integer: n = 50 per group, total sample size N = 100.
#> Reference:
#> Chow, S. C., Shao, J., Wang, H., & Lokhnygina, Y. (2017). Sample Size Calculations in Clinical Research (3rd ed.). CRC Press. Chapter 3 (Comparing Means), Section 3.2.2 noninferiority, Eq 3.12, p. 50.
#> 
#>  Also: Machin et al. (2018) Eq 11.3, p. 173. 
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 

# Bioequivalence of a generic amlodipine: intra-subject CV 25%,
# expected GMR 1.0, 80-125% acceptance range (2x2 crossover)
calculate("bioequivalence", cv = 0.25)
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results
#> • Design type: "Bioequivalence (2x2 crossover, exact TOST integration)"
#> • Required sample size: 12
#> • Total sample size: 24
#> • Power achieved: 0.8372
#> Parameter roles
#> 
#> • cv = intra-subject coefficient of variation (log scale implied)
#> • theta0 = anticipated geometric mean ratio (true ratio, default 1.0)
#> • margin = [0.80, 1.25] average BE criteria
#> • n is per sequence; total subjects = 2n
#> Formula (plain text):
#> `power = E[max(0, Phi((U-mu)/SE-t*sqrt(V/df))-Phi((L-mu)/SE+t*sqrt(V/df)))], V
#> ~ chi-square(df), df=N-2`
#> Formula (LaTeX):
#> $$\mathrm{Power}=E\!\left[\max\!\left\{0,\Phi\!\left(\frac{U-\mu}{SE}-t\sqrt{V/\nu}\right)-\Phi\!\left(\frac{L-\mu}{SE}+t\sqrt{V/\nu}\right)\right\}\right],\quad V\sim\chi^2_\nu,\ \nu=N-2$$ 
#> Calculation process:
#> 
#> • Step 1: Log-scale within-subject SD = sqrt(log(1+CV^2)) = 0.246221;
#> anticipated log ratio = 0.000000.
#> • Step 2: TOST log limits are [-0.223144, 0.223144], each with one-sided alpha
#> 0.0500.
#> • Step 3: Integrate the conditional normal acceptance probability over the
#> chi-square variance estimate (df = N-2); negative-width acceptance intervals
#> contribute zero.
#> • Step 4: Search balanced even totals for the smallest N meeting the target
#> power.
#> • Step 5: n = 12 per sequence, total N = 24, achieved power = 0.837226 (target
#> 0.8000).
#> Reference:
#> Primary: Phillips, K. F. (1990). Power of the two one-sided tests procedure in bioequivalence. Journal of Pharmacokinetics and Biopharmaceutics, 18(2), 137-144.
#> 
#>  Also: Julious, S. A. (2004). Tutorial in biostatistics: sample sizes for clinical trials with normal data. Statistics in Medicine, 23(12), 1921-1986 (Section 6.3 'Cross-over trials', Eq 6.1-6.9; the non-central t power expression is Eq 6.8).
#>  Schuirmann, D. J. (1987). J Pharmacokinet Biopharm, 15(6), 657-680;
#>  Chow & Liu (2009). Design and Analysis of Bioavailability and Bioequivalence Studies. 
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 

# Colorectal cancer screening kit: expected sensitivity 85%,
# CI half-width +/-5%, clinic prevalence 20%
calculate("diagAccuracy", "estimate", "proportion",
  prob = 0.85, d = 0.05, prevalence = 0.20
)
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results
#> • Design type: "Diagnostic accuracy (single)"
#> • Cases needed: 196
#> • Total subjects to screen: 980
#> Formula (plain text):
#> `N_cases = (Z_1-a/2)^2 * P*(1-P)/d^2`
#> Formula (LaTeX):
#> $$n_{{{cases}}} = \frac{Z_{1-\alpha/2}^2 \cdot p(1-p)}{d^2}$$ 
#> Calculation process:
#> 
#> • Step 1: Specify diagnostic accuracy prob (Se or Sp) = 0.85, margin of error d
#> = 0.05, prevalence = 0.20 (alpha = 0.05).
#> • Step 2: Determine critical value: Z_(1-alpha/2) = 1.96 (confidence level =
#> 95%).
#> • Step 3: Calculate target cases required: n_cases = Z_sum^2 * prob * (1 -
#> prob) / d^2 = (1.96)^2 * 0.85 * 0.15 / (0.05)^2 = 195.91.
#> • Step 4: Adjust for disease prevalence: total subjects to screen = n_cases /
#> prevalence = 195.91 / 0.20 = 979.57.
#> • Step 5: Round up to integer: Target cases needed = 196, Total subjects to
#> screen = 980.
#> Reference:
#> Primary: Hanley, J. A., & McNeil, B. J. (1982). The meaning and use of the area under a receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve. Radiology, 143(1), 29-36.
#> 
#> Review: Hajian-Tilaki, K. (2014). Sample size estimation in diagnostic test studies of biomedical informatics. Journal of Biomedical Informatics, 48, 193-204. 
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 

# AUC precision for a biomarker validation cohort: AUC 0.80,
# CI half-width 0.10, 1:1 case:control, binormal variance
calculate("diagAUC", auc = 0.80, d = 0.05, var_method = "binormal")
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> ✔ Sample Size Calculation Results
#> • Design type: "Single-group AUC CI precision"
#> • Cases needed: 184
#> • Controls needed: 184
#> • Total subjects: 368
#> Parameter roles
#> 
#> • auc = anticipated area under the ROC curve
#> • precision = desired CI half-width L
#> • ratio = controls per case (non-cases:cases; default 1)
#> • prevalence = clinical disease proportion; alternative to fixed ratio
#> • screening totals, when present, meet expected case and control quotas, not an
#> assurance probability
#> • var_method = binormal variance function
#> ! The controls:cases ratio fell back to 1 (a 1:1 quota); screening volume requires prevalence in (0, 1).
#> 
#> Formula (plain text):
#> `N_cases = (Z_1-a/2 / d)^2 * V(AUC); controls = ceiling(ceiling(N_cases)*R), R
#> = controls/cases`
#> Formula (LaTeX):
#> $$n_{cases} = \left(\frac{Z_{1-\alpha/2}}{d}\right)^2 \cdot V(AUC), \quad R = n_{controls}/n_{cases}$$ 
#> Calculation process:
#> 
#> • Step 1: Anticipated AUC = 0.80, precision d = 0.05, controls:cases R = 1,
#> alpha = 0.05.
#> • Step 2: Use the binormal variance model: V(AUC) = 0.1195.
#> • Step 3: Calculate cases: n_cases = (Z_(1-alpha/2)/d)^2 * V(AUC) =
#> (1.96/0.05)^2 * 0.1195 = 183.56.
#> • Step 4: Round cases up first: Target cases needed = 184; controls =
#> ceiling(cases*R) = 184.
#> • Step 5: Sum integer quotas: Total subjects = 184 + 184 = 368.
#> Reference:
#> Primary: Zhou, X.-H., Obuchowski, N. A., & McClish, D. K. (2011). Statistical Methods in Diagnostic Medicine (2nd ed.). Wiley. Section 6.1.2, pp. 196-199 (Eq 6.4/6.5/6.6; CTC worked example).
#> 
#>  Original variance: Hanley, J. A., & McNeil, B. J. (1982). Radiology, 143(1), 29-36.
#>  Binormal variance: Obuchowski, N. A. (1994). Computing sample size for receiver operating characteristic studies. Investigative Radiology, 29(2), 238-243. 
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>
